title: What the Evidence Says About Lion’s Mane Mushroom for Patients With Cancer | Oncology Nursing Society
abstract: In a trial involving 77 individuals with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher (age = 53.2 ± 0.7 years), eight weeks of supplementation with lion’s mane extract led to significant improvements in depression (29.4%), anxiety (33.2%), and sleep disorders (39.1%) compared to baseline. In another study, researchers randomized 30 adults aged 50–80 diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment to receive either a placebo or lion’s mane extract powder (four 250 mg tablets taken three times daily) for 16 weeks. Participants randomized to the lion’s mane extract (four 0.8 g supplements daily for 12 weeks) had notable improvements in cognitive function compared to those in the control group. Additionally, researchers conducting a randomized trial of 41 younger adults aged 18–45 years found subjective reductions in stress following 28-day supplementation with a daily dose of 1.8 g of lion’s mane. However, researchers conducting a study of 24 college-age students did not find any effect on cognition after supplementation with 10 g of lion’s mane per day for four weeks.
